Rationale: Empty/whitespace returns Empty; the \\?\ long-path prefix is stripped before the invalid-char scan so its '?' is not rejected while a later '?'/'*' is; drive-relative 'a:b' and rooted-without-drive '\photos' fail IsPathFullyQualified; relative segments are Trim()med so '.. ' is still caught; absolute paths pass as an explicit user choice. Residual lexical gaps (junctions) are closed at run time by GetFullPath+StartsWith and ValidateNoEscapeViaReparsePoint. Tests: ActionDestinationPolicyTests, ActionDestinationRootTests.

Function: ActionDestinationPolicy.public static ActionDestinationCheck ValidateNoEscapeViaReparsePoint( string sourceFolder, string destinationFolderOrPath, IFileSystem fileSystem)
Rationale: Resolves BOTH source folder and destination with fs.ResolveRealPath and fails CLOSED (EscapesSourceFolder) on IOException/UnauthorizedAccessException (RV-S06 link loop); containment uses realSource + separator so C:\ph does not prefix-match C:\photos2; drive-root source 'C:\' trims to 'C:' and re-adds the separator correctly; equal paths are Ok. An ArgumentException (NUL in path) would propagate, but both callers sit inside ExecuteAsync/ExecuteGroupAsync try blocks and fail before any mutation. Tests: DestinationEscapeTests, SymlinkDestinationEscapeNativeTests, PhysicalFileSystemReparseTests.

Function: ActionDestinationPolicy.public static PickedFolderCheck ValidatePickedFolder(string? destination, string photoFolder, Func<string, bool> directoryExists)
Rationale: Reuses Validate and additionally requires IsPathFullyQualified, so a relative or drive-relative pick is NotAbsolute; compares GetFullPath+TrimEndingDirectorySeparator with OrdinalIgnoreCase to catch SameAsPhotoFolder; existence via injected directoryExists (no I/O of its own). null photoFolder/directoryExists throw; an empty photoFolder string would make GetFullPath throw ArgumentException (callers pass the loaded folder). Tests: PickedFolderPolicyTests.

Function: DuplicateFinder.public static async Task<List<string>> FindAsync( IReadOnlyList<string> files, bool removeNumbered, Func<string, CancellationToken, Task<string>> hash, IFileSystem? fileSystem = null, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default)
Rationale: Whole pipeline read: Distinct(OrdinalIgnoreCase) stops a path listed twice from being its own duplicate (on a case-sensitive directory two distinct files differing by case collapse to one, which only under-reports); one stat per candidate; groups keyed size|hash so a weak hash cannot join files of different length; a group where every member matches the naming rule keeps the first (matching.RemoveAt(0)) so a whole content group is never returned; only IO-type exceptions skip a file, OperationCanceledException rethrown. It only returns paths; the caller deletes. See W2-FA-10 for the size-scan lambda ignoring the token. Tests: DuplicateFinderTests, DuplicateFinderSkipsUnremovableGroupsTests, FileActionSafetyEdgeTests.

Task.Run(...) body that stats every candidate: the token is passed only to Task.Run (cancels before start) and the lambda never calls ThrowIfCancellationRequested, so cancelling a scan of thousands of files on a slow share is not honoured until the stat loop finishes (the first check is in the later hash loop). No data risk, wasted I/O and delayed cancel. See W2-FA-10. Test: none found for cancellation during the size scan.

Per-path stat: uses fileSystem.GetFileStat or File.Exists+new FileInfo(path).Length; a file deleted between Exists and Length throws FileNotFoundException (an IOException) which is caught and mapped to size -1; UnauthorizedAccess/Argument/NotSupported also mapped to -1; other exception types propagate. Directory or missing path gives -1.
Filter item.Size >= 0 drops missing or unreadable candidates (-1 sentinel); zero-byte files stay and group together, which is correct because all empty files are identical content.
GroupBy key is the long file size; order inside a group follows the Distinct input order, which the survivor rule (first in input order) later relies on.
group.Count() > 1 discards unique-size files without ever hashing them (minimises disk reads, AGENTS rule 1); a size-unique file can never be a duplicate.
Outer group predicate: group.Any(naming rule matches) skips reading a size group in which no member can ever be selected for removal; correct because hash groups are sub-groups of size groups.

Inner predicate IsMatch(GetFileNameWithoutExtension(path)) == removeNumbered with the pattern ' \(\d+\)$'; extension stripped first so 'a (1).jpg' matches; \d also matches non-ASCII digits, which only widens 'numbered' and still needs identical content plus a surviving member. Same predicate as F01651.
Projection (Size: group.Key, Paths: list) materialises each size group once; no shared mutable state, lists are owned by the result.
Selector item => item.Path inside the group projection; trivial and null-safe because paths come from the Distinct/stat stage.
SelectMany selector expanding each size group into (size, path) pairs in group order; deterministic.
Tuple selector path => (group.Size, path); captures the group's size so the dictionary key size|hash uses the stat-time size.
group.Count > 1 on hash groups: a content group of one is never a duplicate; groups.Values enumeration order is insertion order, so output order is stable.

Selection rule predicate for removal; with removeNumbered=false it selects un-numbered originals, with true the ' (n)' copies; combined with the matching.Count==group.Count guard one member always survives. Same expression as F01645.

Function: FileActionService.public FileActionService( OperationJournal journal, IFileSystem fileSystem, IClock clock, IRecycleBin recycleBin, Func<string, string, Task>? moveOverride = null)
Rationale: Constructor null-checks journal, fileSystem, clock and recycleBin (ArgumentNullException); moveOverride is an optional test/override seam; no I/O. Tests: FileActionServiceTests.
Volatile.Read(_inProgress) != 0; a read of the INV-4 gate flag with correct memory ordering and no side effects.

Interlocked.CompareExchange(0 to 1) is an atomic test-and-set, so two callers cannot both enter (INV-4); the gate is shared with UndoService and RecoveryRetryService through this instance. Tests: CaptureGroupSidecarAndGateTests.

Volatile.Write(0) releases unconditionally with no owner token: only safe because every caller invokes End() solely after a successful TryBegin (verified in ExecuteAsync, ExecuteGroupAsync, RecoveryRetryService, UndoService where the busy return precedes the try/finally).
Forwards !_recycleBin.CanRecycle(path); a pure query used by the App to decide on the permanent-delete confirmation; exceptions from the bin implementation propagate to the caller unchanged.

Function: FileActionService.public async Task<CaptureGroupActionResult> ExecuteGroupAsync( CaptureGroupActionRequest request, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default)
Rationale: Read in full: members are preflighted (existence, destination containment incl. reparse check, destination-exists, bin eligibility) BEFORE the manifest is journaled; a missing partner is skipped and reported; Copy ownership is proven only by CopyCreationProof (R01, fixed by #290/fc1d7a53); Move in-flight ownership uses a pre-stat plus IsDestinationExists; compensation, rolledBack-to-Dismissed and the compensationFailure catch leave Prepared for reconcile; gate released in finally. Defect: request.Group.Paths.Count < 2 throws an English unlocalized ArgumentException whose Message is shown as the failure text (W2-FA-06, likely unreachable from the App); also CreateDirectory(destinationFolder) runs before tx.BeginAsync so a journal append failure leaves an empty folder. Tests: CaptureGroupActionServiceTests, CaptureGroupActionRollbackTests, CopyForeignDestinationTests, FileActionServiceGroupMutationGapTests.

Lambda member => imagePaths.Contains(member.Source): imagePaths is an OrdinalIgnoreCase set built from the group, so the 'at least one photo still exists' check cannot be defeated by casing; guards the sidecar-only case with FileNotFoundException before anything is journaled.

member => member.Permanent inside All(): the group-level Permanent flag is only true when every member is permanent AND at least one exists (All && Any); per-member flags stay in the manifest for Recovery/Undo.
member => member.Permanent inside Any(): second half of the group-level flag expression, guarding the vacuous-truth case of an empty manifest (unreachable because the photo check precedes it).

Task.Run(() => TryCopyNew(source, destination, proof)): proof is a fresh CopyCreationProof per member captured into a local, so the catch block reads DestinationCreated only for the member in flight; a token cancelled before the delegate starts creates nothing; created==false becomes IOException destination-exists without ever claiming the foreign file. Test: CopyForeignDestinationTests.

Task.Run(() => _fileSystem.Move(...)): relies on Move not overwriting (throws on an existing destination), which the IsDestinationExists filter then classifies as foreign; cancellation only takes effect before the delegate starts, after which the move completes and is verified.

Task.Run(() => DeletePermanently): reachable only for a member whose Permanent flag was set at preflight, which requires AllowPermanentDelete; followed by a FileExists check throwing SourceStillExistsAfterRecovery. Never exercised against a real bin (fakes only).

Task.Run(() => SendToRecycleBin): followed by FileExists check; overflow that would silently become a permanent delete is pre-empted by RecycleBinCapacity.FirstOverflow before the Prepared line is written.
member => new CaptureGroupMemberResult(member, true, false): on the success path every manifest member passed its own verification inside the loop, so reporting all as Completed is accurate.
member => member.Permanent in Any(): PermanentlyDeleted is true when any member was permanently deleted, matching UndoService.RegisterGroup which treats permanence per member.

Compensation delegate dispatching RemoveCreatedCopies (Copy) or RestoreMovedMembers (Move) on the pool; deliberately has no cancellation token so a cancelled action still rolls back; reads inFlightCopyProof.DestinationCreated and inFlightDestinationIsOurs after the loop has ended, so there is no concurrent writer; IO-type failures are counted as stuck, other types reach the compensationFailure catch.
member => InspectGroupMember(operation, member, ex.Message): evaluated after compensation against the real disk; InspectGroupMember converts IO-type errors into StateKnown:false.

Predicate for rolledBack requires StateKnown, !Completed, !Conflict, SourceExists and !DestinationExists for EVERY member, so any unknown or half-done member keeps a Failed Recovery line instead of a terminal Dismissed (conservative).
member => member.Completed && member.Member.Permanent: PermanentlyDeleted on a failed Recycle group counts only completed permanent members, so a refused permanent delete is not reported as done.

Compensation-failure result: every member is reported Completed=false, Conflict=true, StateKnown=false with the original ex.Message; no outcome line is written so Prepared remains for startup reconcile. For a Recycle that actually completed this under-reports, but StateKnown=false tells the App not to trust it. Test: CaptureGroupActionRollbackTests.

Function: FileActionService.private int RemoveCreatedCopies(IReadOnlyList<JournalGroupMember> done, JournalGroupMember? inFlight, bool inFlightDestinationIsOurs)
Rationale: Deletes a done copy only if its length still equals the manifest size (a changed file is kept and counted stuck), and the in-flight destination only when CopyCreationProof said this operation created it; deletion uses Delete then FileExists to confirm; IO/Unauthorized/Argument/NotSupported caught per member; sources and bin never touched; reverse order. R01 foreign-destination case is covered. Tests: CaptureGroupActionRollbackTests, CopyForeignDestinationTests.

Function: FileActionService.private int RestoreMovedMembers(IReadOnlyList<JournalGroupMember> done, JournalGroupMember? inFlight, bool inFlightDestinationIsOurs)
Rationale: Moves a done member back only when its source is absent and MatchesMovedDestination (size and within 2 s) holds; the in-flight member's partial destination is deleted only if inFlightDestinationIsOurs, source still exactly the manifest file and destination strictly shorter than the source (a full-size destination is left for Recovery); Move has no overwrite, so a new file at the source makes it stuck rather than lost; stuck count is surfaced in the message. Tests: CaptureGroupActionRollbackTests, FileActionServiceGroupMutationGapTests.
Throws coded VerifySizeChanged when the destination stat is null or its length differs from the manifest size; size-only by design (destination volume may restamp the write time).

Move verification: source must be gone (MoveSourceNotRemoved otherwise) and then VerifyGroupDestination; a file recreated at the source in the window makes a completed Move report failure, which is the conservative direction.

Function: FileActionService.private CaptureGroupMemberResult InspectGroupMember(FileOperationType operation, JournalGroupMember member, string error)
Rationale: Post-state per member: Recycle = source missing (Conflict if present but changed); Move completed = source absent and dest length == size, source compared with the tolerant moved-file fingerprint; Copy exact; conflict = !completed && (!sourceUnchanged || destination present); nullable comparison destination?.Length == member.Size is false for null; IO-type errors give StateKnown:false. Move completed uses size only, so a foreign same-size destination would read as completed (minor, only reached on the failure path). Test: CaptureGroupActionRollbackTests.

Function: FileActionService.public async Task<FileActionResult> ExecuteAsync(FileActionRequest request, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default)
Rationale: Single-file path reviewed fully: destination policy, reparse check, FileExists(destination) before journaling, CreateDirectory only after all pre-checks, Prepared before mutation, VerifyMoved/VerifyDestination, Commit failure reported as JournalPersisted=false, catch computes SourceRemoved from disk, copy cleanup gated by CopyCreationProof (R01 fixed). Open P3 (W2-FA-09): unlike the group path a failed single Move has no partial-destination cleanup, and a successful SendToRecycleBin/DeletePermanently is not re-checked with FileExists (the group path does); WindowsRecycleBin.SendToRecycleBin currently throws if the file is still there, so this is defence in depth. Tests: FileActionServiceTests, FileActionServiceSingleMutationGapTests, FileActionSafetyEdgeTests, CrashMatrixTests.

Task.Run(() => TryCopyNew(source, destinationPath, copyProof)): copyProof is a single instance read in the catch block after the awaited task has finished, so there is no race; created==false is an IOException that leaves the foreign destination alone (RemovePartialCopy not called because DestinationCreated stays false). Test: CopyForeignDestinationTests.

Task.Run(() => _fileSystem.Move(source, destinationPath)): a token cancelled before start yields OperationCanceledException with nothing touched, which the catch turns into a Dismissed line via IsUntouched; once started the Move completes and is verified.

Task.Run(() => DeletePermanently(source)): only when permanent (bin cannot take the path) AND request.AllowPermanentDelete, both enforced before the Prepared line; the Prepared entry already carries Permanent=true so Recovery reports PermanentlyDeleted.

Task.Run(() => SendToRecycleBin(source)) followed directly by MarkMutationCompleted with no FileExists(source) re-check (the group path throws SourceStillExistsAfterRecovery in that case); correctness depends on the IRecycleBin contract (WindowsRecycleBin throws CoreRecycleNotDeleted when the file is still present, other implementations unverified). See W2-FA-09.

Function: FileActionService.private void RemovePartialCopy(string destination, long sourceSize)
Rationale: Forwards to PartialDestinationCleanup.RemoveIfPartial; both callers (ExecuteAsync catch, group compensation) call it only when CopyCreationProof.DestinationCreated, so it can only delete a file this operation created.

Function: FileActionService.private bool IsUntouched(string source, long size, DateTime lastWriteUtc, string? destination)
Rationale: Exact same-volume compare of source length and LastWriteUtc plus destination absent; any non-OOM exception returns false so the Failed line is kept; used only to decide Dismissed versus Failed after a pre-start cancel. Test: FileActionServiceSingleMutationGapTests.

Returns !FileExists(source); IO/Unauthorized/Argument/NotSupported map to false (not gone) so a stat error never removes a photo from the catalog; runs inside the catch block, so any other exception type would escape ExecuteAsync, but FileExists on the real file system does not throw those.

Function: FileActionService.private static bool IsSamePath(string first, string second)
Rationale: GetFullPath + TrimEndingDirectorySeparator + OrdinalIgnoreCase; does not resolve junctions, 8.3 names or UNC aliases, but an alias of the same folder makes the destination file equal the source, which the later FileExists(destination) check rejects, so the source is never overwritten.

Function: FileFingerprint.public static bool MatchesMovedDestination(FileStat stat, long size, DateTime recordedUtc)
Rationale: Null-checks stat, requires equal length and |delta mtime| <= 2 s (FAT rounding) using tick arithmetic; used only on the moved-destination side (callers keep plain equality for same-volume files); a false match needs a same-size file written within 2 s of the original. Test: FileActionsSmallMutationGapTests.

Pass 1/2/3 verified against OperationJournal.ComputeLatestEntries and the tail-window rule: only lines strictly before a Committed/Dismissed latest line are dropped, unparseable lines are kept verbatim, last 200 committed Moves kept. Gap (W2-FA-04): it drops an earlier Prepared line that carries GroupMembers, which is the only evidence RepairGroupLinesSettledByOlderBuild (groupHistory in ReconcilePendingOperations) uses to detect a group settled by an older build; the class comment lists four readers but not that one. Reachable when repair's append failed (TryReconcileAppend returned false) and JournalStartupRecovery still compacts. Tests: JournalCompactionPlanTests, JournalCompactionPlanReprepareTests, JournalGroupDowngradeTests (survives compaction for this build's lines only).

IsDroppable: blank lines dropped, unparseable kept, Prepared/Failed latest ids never dropped, lines before a Committed/Dismissed latest dropped unless in the committedMoveWindow; latest[entry.Id] always exists because the FA-01 skip only happens when a previous entry exists. Same W2-FA-04 gap: a Prepared-with-members line before a members-less Committed (older-build verdict) is dropped, erasing the downgrade evidence.

Strips one trailing '\n' then one '\r', exactly the terminator handling of StreamReader.ReadLine for the common cases; a lone inner '\r' is separately excluded from recognition in Build, so both readers agree on every entry the plan recognises.
code is not null && ContainsKey on an ordinal FrozenDictionary; null-safe, no exceptions. Test: JournalErrorCatalogTests.

Resolves through BuiltInCatalog.EnglishLocalizer so persisted text is language-invariant; an unknown code throws ArgumentException (programming error, codes are constants). Test: JournalErrorCatalogTests.
Same lookup with Localizer.Current for UI text; unknown code throws ArgumentException, only called with the constants or a code from JournalCodedException.

Function: JournalErrors.public static string? Describe(string? code, string? storedText)
Rationale: Known code gives localized text; unknown code, null code, or old record returns the stored text unchanged and never throws, so records from newer or older builds still display. Test: JournalErrorCodeTests.
Null-guards the entry and forwards (ErrorCode, Error) to Describe(code, text).

Function: JournalErrors.internal static (string? Code, string Text) ForJournal(Exception ex)
Rationale: JournalCodedException with a KNOWN code gives (code, English text); any OperationCanceledException (including TaskCanceledException) gives CancelledByUser; everything else keeps ex.Message with no code (OS text, possibly in the OS language, as documented); a coded exception built with the default constructor has Code="" and falls to the message branch. Test: JournalErrorCodeTests.

Function: JournalErrors.private static string Text(Localizer localizer, string code)
Rationale: Null code throws ArgumentNullException, unknown code throws ArgumentException with the code in the message; known code resolves the key through the supplied localizer.

Base message is LocalizedText(code), so constructing with an unknown code throws ArgumentException instead of producing an exception with a bogus code; Code is stored for ForJournal. Test: JournalErrorCodeTests.
Parameterless constructor (CA1032 pattern) sets Code to empty string; ForJournal's IsKnown("") is false so it degrades to the message branch.

Function: JournalCodedException.public JournalCodedException(string message, Exception innerException) : base(message, innerException)
Rationale: (message, innerException) constructor sets Code to empty; same degradation as the parameterless one, preserving the inner exception.

Null-guards the line, resets the per-thread t_type/t_state tri-state before deserialising and returns null only for JsonException (malformed JSON, overflowing numbers, invalid dates, depth limit). Acceptance defects live in IsKnown/RecordingConverter.Read (W2-FA-01), not here. Tests: JournalLineParserTests, JournalGroupSchemaTests.

UTF-8 span overload with the same reset/catch discipline; invalid UTF-8 surfaces as JsonException and is rejected; used by the tail reader and compaction plan so all readers share one acceptance rule. Tests: JournalLineParserTests, JournalTailCommittedMoveTests.

Reads the thread-static recognition flags immediately after Deserialize on the same thread (no await in between), so another thread's parse cannot interfere; requires Type and State recognised, non-empty Id, usable Source and valid group members, then normalises Destination.
Rejects null/whitespace and NUL; does not reject other invalid path characters, which .NET file queries tolerate (they only throw for NUL). Test: JournalBlankPathTests.
A blank or NUL Destination becomes null via a record 'with', matching what readers assume (no destination); a usable Destination is returned unchanged.

Rejects a null member or a blank member Source but not a member Source/Destination containing NUL, unlike the entry-level IsUsablePath. A corrupt line with such a member reaches IsGroupMemberCompleted/GetFileStat (PhysicalFileSystem.GetFileStat uses new FileInfo(path), expected to throw ArgumentException) and, in RepairGroupLinesSettledByOlderBuild, that exception is outside any try/catch. Not reproduced (needs a NUL in a journal group member). See W2-FA-07. Tests: JournalBlankPathTests, JournalGroupSchemaTests (neither covers NUL in a member).

Lambda member => member is not null && !IsNullOrWhiteSpace(member.Source): correct for null and blank, silent about NUL characters in Source and in the member's Destination (never validated). Same W2-FA-07 trace as HasValidGroupMembers.

Function: JournalLineParser.private static bool IsKnown<T>(ref Utf8JsonReader reader, string? alias) where T : struct, Enum
Rationale: Uses Enum.TryParse<T>(text.Trim(), ignoreCase) which, even for a non-[Flags] enum, accepts comma lists and ORs the values (Move,Recycle gives 2; Prepared,Committed gives 1, a defined value) so the check says 'recognised', but LenientEnumConverter.ParseText only looks up single names and returns the default (Move/Prepared) for such text. Reproduced (W2-FA-01): Type='Move,Recycle' accepted as Move, State='Prepared,Committed' accepted as Prepared. Corrupt/hand-edited journal only, writer never emits it. Tests: JournalLineParserTests (no comma-list case).

HandleNull=true so a JSON null for Type/State reaches Read and is recorded as present-but-unrecognised (2), matching the old JsonValueKind.Null rejection; without it the converter would be skipped and the flag would stay 'missing', which is also rejected, so both routes reject.

Function: JournalLineParser.RecordingConverter.public override T Read(ref Utf8JsonReader reader, Type typeToConvert, JsonSerializerOptions options)
Rationale: Records known=1/2 from IsKnown and then delegates the value to LenientEnumConverter, so its recognition and its value can disagree (W2-FA-01): a comma-list that IsKnown accepts is read as the default member, inventing e.g. a pending Move/Prepared line. Duplicate members: last occurrence wins for both flag and value, as intended.

Function: JournalLineParser.RecordingConverter.public override void Write(Utf8JsonWriter writer, T value, JsonSerializerOptions options)
Rationale: Write forwards to LenientEnumConverter.Write (writes the enum name); never used by the journal writer, which serialises with default options and the enums' own [JsonConverter] attribute, so no divergence in what is written.

Function: JournalStartupRecovery.public static async Task<IReadOnlyList<JournalEntry>> RunAsync( OperationJournal journal, IClock clock, ILog? log = null)
Rationale: Captures startedUtc before Task.Run so actions started during reconcile are excluded; reconcile then Compact run on the pool; returns only entries that became Failed; any exception (locked journal, ArgumentException from a bad line escaping repair) is logged and returns an empty list, never crashing startup. A reconcile exception also skips Compact for that start (see W2-FA-07). Tests: JournalStartupRecoveryTests.

Pool lambda: ReconcilePendingOperations(preparedBeforeUtc) then Compact(journal, log) then returns the reconcile result; compaction runs even when repair's append failed (relevant to W2-FA-04) but is skipped if reconcile throws.
entry => entry.State == JournalState.Failed: selects only reconcile verdicts that need user attention; Committed outcomes are only counted in the log line.

Function: JournalStartupRecovery.private static void Compact(OperationJournal journal, ILog? log)
Rationale: Never throws: any exception from TryCompact is logged and ignored (journal untouched because the atomic rename is the last step); Compacted/Failed/Busy/Changed are logged with invariant-culture numbers; NotSupported/BelowThreshold/NotWorthIt fall through silently. Tests: JournalCompactionTests, JournalStartupRecoveryTests.

Function: JournalTransaction.public JournalTransaction(OperationJournal journal, IClock clock, JournalEntry prepared, JournalEntry? retryOf = null)
Rationale: Stores journal/clock/prepared/retryOf with no null checks; internal sealed class with three in-repo callers that always pass non-null values, so a missing check cannot be hit from outside.

Fast durability appends inline and returns a completed task; PowerLossSafe wraps Begin in Task.Run so the mutation still starts only after Prepared is durable; exceptions travel through the task. Tests: JournalDurabilityTests, JournalTransactionTests.
Begin throws InvalidOperationException only when TryBegin reports Superseded, which can only happen with retryOf; non-retry callers can never see it.

Takes the live marker BEFORE the Prepared append (so a reconcile that can read the line can see the marker), releases it and rethrows if the append throws, releases and sets Superseded when a retry's conditional append is refused, and sets IsPrepared only after the append succeeded. Tests: LiveOperationMarkerTests, RecoveryRetryRaceTests.
Swaps the field to null before disposing, so a second call (Commit then Dispose) is a no-op and a throwing registry Dispose cannot run twice.
Forwards to ReleaseLiveMarker so every exit path (including cancellation before an outcome) frees the live marker; idempotent.

Function: JournalTransaction.public void VerifyDestination(IFileSystem fileSystem, string destination, string errorCode)
Rationale: Throws the supplied coded error when the destination is missing or its length differs from the prepared size, and sets MutationCompleted only after that check passes, so a failed verify never reports success.

Function: JournalTransaction.public void VerifyMoved(IFileSystem fileSystem, string source, string destination, string sizeErrorCode)
Rationale: Move check: source must be gone (MoveSourceNotRemoved, destination copy is kept and never deleted) and then VerifyDestination; a file created at the source in the window reports failure on an otherwise complete move, the conservative direction.
Sets MutationCompleted for operations with nothing to verify (Recycle); called only after the bin call returned.

Builds Committed, takes the timestamp from the clock inside the try so a clock failure is a journal failure (Prepared remains for reconcile) and not a thrown exception that would make the caller write Failed for a completed operation; releases the live marker only after the append attempt; the entry is returned even when the append failed (callers read journalError). Tests: JournalCommitClockFailureTests, JournalTransactionTests.

Function: JournalTransaction.public JournalEntry? Fail(Exception failure, out string? journalError)
Rationale: Maps the exception through JournalErrors.ForJournal (code+English or CancelledByUser) and delegates to AppendFailureOutcome(Failed). Tests: JournalErrorCodeTests.
Writes a terminal Dismissed line with null Error/ErrorCode for a fully rolled back operation; old builds read Dismissed as cleared, never as unfinished.

Function: JournalTransaction.private JournalEntry? AppendFailureOutcome(JournalState state, string? errorText, string? errorCode, out string? journalError)
Rationale: Not prepared and not a retry: releases marker, writes nothing, returns null; retry: AppendIfUnchangedSince(retryOf, [own Prepared] or [], failed) and Superseded when refused; append exceptions captured into journalError; marker released in finally only after the outcome attempt; returns null when superseded or the append failed so callers never treat an unwritten line as journaled. Tests: JournalTransactionTests, RecoveryRetryRaceTests.

Custom value equality over every field plus SequenceEqual on GroupMembers (record equality of JournalGroupMember), needed because journal reads build fresh lists; DateTime compared with == (ticks, Kind ignored, consistent with round-tripped UTC values). Test: JournalModelTests.
Hashes the same fields as Equals (ordinal strings, members in order); DateTime.GetHashCode ignores Kind just like ==, so equal entries hash equally.

Function: JournalEntry.private static bool MembersEqual(IReadOnlyList<JournalGroupMember>? left, IReadOnlyList<JournalGroupMember>? right)
Rationale: Null on either side equal only when both null; otherwise SequenceEqual, so an absent list differs from an empty one.

Function: OperationJournal.public OperationJournal(IAppPaths paths, IFileSystem fileSystem, IClock clock, Func<JournalDurability>? durability = null, Action<TimeSpan>? appendRetryDelay = null, ILiveOperationRegistry? liveOperations = null, IJournalCompactionFiles? compactionFiles = null)
Rationale: Null-checks paths, fileSystem and clock; durability provider defaults to Fast, append retry delay to Thread.Sleep, live registry to the in-process one, compaction primitives to null (never compacts); _path from paths.JournalFile. Tests: OperationJournalGapTests.
Default durability provider lambda returns Fast; only used when the caller passes none.
Default FlushToDisk lambda does fs.Flush(flushToDisk: true) (fsync); replaced by a test seam only. Test: OperationJournalDurableFlushTests.
Re-evaluates the provider on every read so a Settings change applies to the next write without restart.
Returns the injected registry; shared by transactions and reconcile so the live marker contract holds.
Null-guards and appends a single line through AppendLines under the journal lock.

Under _gate re-reads the latest state and dismisses an entry only when the current latest equals the caller's snapshot (R09), skipped entries are returned instead of silently hidden; Dismissed lines keep GroupMembers; one batched write; timestamp captured before the lock. Atomic per instance only (documented best effort across processes). Dismissing a Prepared entry that another process is still executing is not blocked, but the owner's later Committed supersedes it. Tests: JournalReconcileRaceTests, OperationJournalGapTests.

No file or zero length returns false; reads the last byte through a shared read handle; called while this process holds the append handle (FileShare.Read for others), so the tail cannot change before the write; non-seekable stream treated as no repair needed. Test: JournalAppendRobustnessTests.

Lock held across CreateDirectory, serialise, OpenAppendWithRetry, tail repair, one Write and (durable) fsync; a torn previous line is isolated by a leading newline. Defect (W2-FA-03): JsonSerializer.Serialize silently replaces an unpaired UTF-16 surrogate in a path with U+FFFD (reproduced), so the journal records a Source/Destination that is not the real file; later Recovery/reconcile of that line judges a non-existent path (never acts on the wrong file, but cannot recover the real one). Windows allows unpaired surrogates in file names. Tests: JournalAppendRobustnessTests, JournalConcurrencyTests.

Retries only IOException with HResult 0x80070020/0x80070021, at most 5 attempts with 10,20,30,40 ms backoff (about 100 ms) via the injectable delay, then the exception propagates; the Thread.Sleep runs on the caller thread by documented design. Tests: JournalAppendRobustnessTests, JournalConcurrencyTests.
Compares HResult to the unchecked-cast sharing/lock violation codes; any other IOException (disk full, access denied) is not retried.

Under the lock checks existence and size: 1 MiB or more uses the reverse tail reader (last 200 committed Moves), smaller journals are read in full; the result includes Undo=true Move lines (callers use it only as UndoService's fingerprint fallback). The stream is closed before ReadEntries re-locks. Tests: JournalTailCommittedMoveTests.
Filter entry.Type == Move && State == Committed; Copy/Recycle lines and non-Committed states excluded.

Boundary logic verified: each pass reads [start, boundary), leaves a cut head line to the next pass, doubles the window, stops at 200 entries or start==0, and widens when a single line exceeds the window. Caveats: (int)(boundary-start) overflows for a journal over 2 GiB (unreachable in practice) and ReadExactly can throw EndOfStreamException if another process compacts the file underneath it (the only caller, UndoService fallback, catches Exception). Tests: OperationJournalCompactionBoundaryTests, JournalTailCommittedMoveTests.

Function: OperationJournal.private static List<JournalEntry> ParseCommittedMoves(byte[] buffer, int offset)
Rationale: Splits on '\n' with the vectorised IndexOf, strips a trailing '\r', delegates to the shared tail predicate; a torn last line fails parsing and is skipped.

Skips lines containing the compact Recycle/Copy Type token without parsing, otherwise parses with the shared JournalLineParser rule and keeps only committed Moves, so a quarantined group line can never reach Undo or compaction; shares the comma-list acceptance flaw W2-FA-01 through the parser only. Tests: JournalTailCommittedMoveTests.

Byte search for the exact tokens "Type":"Recycle" and "Type":"Copy"; quotes inside string values are escaped in JSON so these tokens cannot occur inside a Move line's strings, so a Move line is never skipped.
One pass via ComputeLatestEntries; Prepared first then Failed, order = dictionary insertion order (first appearance of each Id), so older items stay first; Dismissed/Committed excluded.
Predicate entry.State == Prepared for the Recovery list head.
Predicate entry.State == Failed for the Recovery list tail.

Function: OperationJournal.private Dictionary<string, JournalEntry> ComputeLatestEntries(Dictionary<string, (string? GroupId, IReadOnlyList<JournalGroupMember> Members)>? groupHistory = null)
Rationale: Single implementation of the latest-line rule with the FA-01 exception; groupHistory records the last line that carries members per Id, which is the evidence used by the downgrade repair. Tests: JournalGroupDowngradeTests.

For each parsed entry skips it as latest when it is a stale reconcile Failed after a Committed (previous read from the dictionary), otherwise overwrites; assignment keeps the key's first-insertion position, preserving ordering.

Function: OperationJournal.private static bool IsStaleReconcileAfterCommitted(JournalEntry entry, JournalEntry? previous)
Rationale: State==Failed && reconcile code && previous Committed: an owner's genuine failure cannot follow its own Committed, so only a late cross-process reconcile verdict is discarded. Test: JournalReconcileRaceTests.

True for PendingUnconfirmed and SourceStillExistsAfterRecovery only; both are written by reconcile (and by the group Recycle owner before any Committed, which is why the rule requires a previous Committed).

Holds the journal lock while streaming lines with StreamReader (UTF-8, BOM detection, lenient decoding, ReadLine also splits on a lone CR) and passes each accepted entry to the handler; unparseable lines are skipped; the handler runs under the lock (all handlers are non-reentrant lookups or Append which re-enters the same lock). A missing file is an empty journal.

Per-entry try/catch (non-OOM) protects each ReconcileOne, and the cutoff skips entries prepared at or after startup. But RepairGroupLinesSettledByOlderBuild(...) is called OUTSIDE that try block and its IsGroupMemberCompleted calls (GetFileStat on member paths) are unguarded, so an ArgumentException from one corrupt group line aborts the whole reconcile (and, in JournalStartupRecovery, the compaction) on every start. Not reproduced. See W2-FA-07. Tests: JournalGroupReconcileTests, JournalReconcileRaceTests, CrashMatrixTests.
Predicate entry.State == Prepared over the latest-entry map, materialised with ToList() before mutation so appends during the loop cannot invalidate the enumeration.

Function: OperationJournal.private void ReconcileOne(JournalEntry pending, List<JournalEntry> reconciled)
Rationale: Skips live operations first; group lines Committed only when EVERY member is complete, otherwise Failed; single Recycle is Failed while the source still exists; Move needs source gone and destination size match, Copy only the destination size; outcomes appended through AppendIfStillPending. Size-only destination match can accept a foreign same-size file (reconcile verdict only, nothing is moved). Tests: JournalGroupReconcileTests, CrashMatrixTests.
member => IsGroupMemberCompleted(pending, member) inside All(); only evaluated when GroupMembers.Count > 0, so All() is never vacuously true.
Closure () => AppendIfStillPending(entry) for the group branch; captures the branch-local entry (not a loop variable) and executes immediately inside TryReconcileAppend.
Same closure for the single Recycle branch; entry local to its branch.
Same closure for the Move/Copy branch; entry local to its branch.

Function: OperationJournal.private void RepairGroupLinesSettledByOlderBuild( Dictionary<string, JournalEntry> latestEntries, Dictionary<string, (string? GroupId, IReadOnlyList<JournalGroupMember> Members)> groupHistory, List<JournalEntry> reconciled)
Rationale: Logic checked: a latest line without members while an earlier line had them is restored with the members; Prepared is re-queued for normal reconcile; Committed is re-verified per member and downgraded to Failed with SettledByOlderBuildText; Dismissed skipped; appends are conditional (AppendIfLatestIs). Two gaps: members.All(IsGroupMemberCompleted) has no exception guard (W2-FA-07) and the evidence it needs can be removed by compaction (W2-FA-04). Tests: JournalGroupDowngradeTests, JournalGroupOlderBuildFixtureTests.
member => IsGroupMemberCompleted(restored, member): per-member disk check used to decide whether a Committed verdict from an older build still holds; throwing behaviour covered under W2-FA-07.
Closure () => AppendIfLatestIs(latest, outcome) captures the per-iteration locals and runs immediately inside TryReconcileAppend.

Function: OperationJournal.private static bool TryReconcileAppend(Func<bool> append, string id)
Rationale: Catches only IOException and UnauthorizedAccessException, logs via the static FileLog and returns false so one failed append leaves that entry Prepared for the next start without losing the already-reconciled list; other exception types propagate to the caller's guards.

Function: OperationJournal.private bool AppendIfLatestIs(JournalEntry expected, JournalEntry outcome)
Rationale: Under the lock recomputes the id's latest line with the same FA-01 rule and appends only if it still equals the snapshot, so a concurrent retry/owner line is never overwritten; plain Append re-enters the same lock.
ReadEntries callback keeping the latest line of the id, skipping a stale reconcile Failed after Committed via IsStaleReconcileAfterCommitted(entry, current).

Function: OperationJournal.private bool IsGroupMemberCompleted(JournalEntry group, JournalGroupMember member)
Rationale: Recycle: not-exists (or exists for an Undo group); Move: !sourceExists && destination size match; Copy: destination size match; blank Destination yields no stat; Undo groups are journaled in undo direction so no swap is needed. GetFileStat/FileExists are unguarded, so a NUL in a corrupt member path can throw ArgumentException out of this method (W2-FA-07). Size-only destination match, as in the single-entry reconcile.

Under the lock re-reads the id's last line and appends only if it is still Prepared and the id is not live (re-checked after the re-read because a retry's marker precedes its Prepared line); a stale Failed after Committed makes latest != Prepared so nothing is appended. Test: LiveOperationMarkerTests.
Callback records the last line of the id (no FA-01 filtering needed because only 'is the last line still Prepared' matters).

Function: OperationJournal.internal bool AppendIfUnchangedSince(JournalEntry anchor, IReadOnlyList<JournalEntry> ownSince, JournalEntry entry)
Rationale: Compares the id's whole history against anchor + exactly ownSince (value equality via the custom Equals); anchor absent means the whole history counts as 'since'; any extra line (another process's Prepared/Committed/Failed) returns false and appends nothing, which is how a loser's Failed can never land after a winner's Committed. Tests: RecoveryRetryRaceTests, JournalReconcileRaceTests.
Callback collecting every entry of the anchor's id in file order for the history comparison.
e => e == anchor used by FindLastIndex: record == routes to the custom Equals, so freshly parsed entries match the snapshot.
Null-guards the id and returns the effective latest line under the lock with the same FA-01 rule as the other readers; used by UndoService settle re-anchoring.
Callback keeping the latest non-stale line for the id.

Re-verified the protocol: snapshot cut at the last '\n' (a torn tail belongs to the delta), plan, staged replacement fsynced, then under the lock open DENYING writers (Busy if an append is in flight), re-read, require the snapshot prefix to be byte-identical (Changed otherwise), copy the delta (adding a newline to a torn tail), fsync, one atomic ReplaceAtomically; only I/O exceptions are mapped to Failed (others propagate; startup's Compact wrapper catches them). Correctness of which lines the plan drops is W2-FA-04. Tests: JournalCompactionTests, OperationJournalCompactionBoundaryTests, JournalConcurrencyTests.

Reads the stream into a MemoryStream sized min(Length,int.MaxValue) and returns ToArray; correct for the journal sizes involved (compaction threshold 1 MiB); a journal over 2 GiB would throw, treated as a Failed compaction.

Deletes only files matching <journal>.*.compact.tmp whose name really ends with the suffix (8.3 guard) and whose last write is older than 1 hour, i.e. only abandoned replacement files created by this feature; Delete failures (still open) are ignored.
Forwards to ILiveOperationRegistry.IsLive(operationId); the cross-process marker check used before any slow file inspection.

Function: OperationJournal.private JournalEntry WithOutcome(JournalEntry pending, JournalState state, string failureCode)
Rationale: Copies the pending entry with the new state, clock timestamp and, for Failed only, the reconcile code with its English text (invariant journal text); Committed clears Error/ErrorCode; EnglishText throws only for an unknown code, and callers pass the two constants.

Function: PartialDestinationCleanup.public static void RemoveIfPartial(IFileSystem fileSystem, string destination, long sourceSize)
Rationale: Deletes the destination only when GetFileStat shows length strictly below the source size (a complete file is left to Recovery) and swallows every non-OOM exception so cleanup never masks the original failure; callers invoke it only after CopyCreationProof.DestinationCreated, so a foreign file is not touched (R01). No dedicated test class; covered through CopyForeignDestinationTests and FileActionServiceSingleMutationGapTests.
Expression property: Destination is Missing and its parent folder no longer exists; null Destination (Recycle) pattern-fails to false, so no NRE.
GroupMembers is non-null with Count > 0; consistent with the dispatch in Check().
Forwards Check.Source of the per-member result; always non-null (CheckPath/record).
Forwards Check.Destination, null for Recycle members or members without a Destination.
Forwards Check.Verdict, i.e. the per-member verdict (possibly overridden for an Undo Recycle group).
Null-checks the IFileSystem; the class only reads (GetFileStat/DirectoryExists) so it cannot mutate disk or journal. Tests: RecoveryFileCheckTests.

Group entries: per-member check, aggregate verdict, top-level Source/Destination taken from the first member; single entries: source compared on size and last-write, destination on size only (cross-volume copies may restamp). Read-only. Tests: RecoveryFileCheckTests, RecoveryFileCheckMutationTests.
member => CheckGroupMember(entry, member) over the member list; evaluated eagerly with ToArray so file-system reads happen once.

Function: RecoveryFileCheck.private RecoveryGroupMemberCheck CheckGroupMember(JournalEntry group, JournalGroupMember member)
Rationale: Re-runs Check on a synthetic single entry (members cleared, Undo cleared, Permanent copied) and, for an Undo Recycle group, overrides the verdict from the source only: Exists with equal size and last-write is AlreadyDone, Exists otherwise Conflict, Missing RecycleUnverifiable, else Unknown. Test: RecoveryFileCheckMutationTests.

Function: RecoveryFileCheck.private static RecoveryVerdict AggregateGroupVerdict(JournalEntry entry, IReadOnlyList<RecoveryGroupMemberCheck> members)
Rationale: Verified every rule against the documented table. Defect (W2-FA-02, reproduced): for an Undo Recycle group in which EVERY member is back at its original path (verdicts all AlreadyDone) none of the Undo/Recycle rules fire and the generic rule at lines 163-170 returns RecycleUnverifiable for Type==Recycle, so Recovery says 'probably in the Recycle Bin, cannot verify' for files that are in fact restored (AlreadyDone / dismiss is the correct verdict). No data loss. Tests: RecoveryFileCheckMutationTests asserts only the per-member verdicts for this case.
member => member.Check.Verdict projection to an array used by all subsequent rules.
Predicate verdict is CanRetry or AlreadyDone for the Undo Move rule; the rule additionally requires at least one CanRetry so an all-AlreadyDone undo falls through to the generic AlreadyDone result.
Predicate RecycleUnverifiable or AlreadyDone for the Undo Recycle retry rule (still needs one RecycleUnverifiable to return CanRetry).

Predicate NotRecycled, RecycleUnverifiable or PermanentlyDeleted for the non-undo Delete retry rule; a Changed present member gives Conflict-like NotRecycled with Changed status handled in the next lambdas.
member => member.Verdict == NotRecycled: selects the members still on disk that a retry would recycle.
member => member.Source.Status == Exists: retry allowed only if every still-present member matches its journaled fingerprint (Changed blocks the retry). Test: RecoveryRecycleGroupTests.

Predicate AlreadyDone or RecycleUnverifiable or PermanentlyDeleted: it is the one that also swallows the 'Undo Recycle, all members AlreadyDone' case and then maps it to RecycleUnverifiable at line 169 (W2-FA-02, reproduced). For non-undo groups the predicate is right.
verdict == PermanentlyDeleted: whole capture unrecoverable only when every member was deleted permanently.
Predicate AlreadyDone or CanRetry for the generic Move/Copy retry rule, with a required CanRetry member; a Conflict/SourceChanged member prevents it (checked by RecoveryFileCheckMutationTests).

Function: RecoveryFileCheck.internal static RecoveryVerdict Decide(JournalEntry entry, RecoveryPathCheck source, RecoveryPathCheck? destination)
Rationale: Matrix re-derived: Recycle ignores state (Missing gives PermanentlyDeleted or RecycleUnverifiable, Unreadable Unknown, else NotRecycled); no destination gives Unknown; Committed gives AlreadyDone/Lost/Unknown; only Prepared/Failed continue; Copy with source and destination both Exists is AlreadyDone, source Changed with a present destination is Conflict, missing source with a Changed destination is DestinationChanged. Internal static, pure. Tests: RecoveryFileCheckTests, RecoveryFileCheckMutationTests.

Function: RecoveryFileCheck.private RecoveryPathCheck CheckPath(string path, long recordedSize, DateTime recordedLastWriteUtc, bool compareLastWrite)
Rationale: Folder existence via DirectoryExists(GetDirectoryName(path)) then GetFileStat; Changed when length differs (or last-write for the source); Unauthorized/IO/Argument/NotSupported (including empty path from GetDirectoryName) map to Unreadable with the folder flag computed so far. Test: RecoveryRetryFileCheckFaultTests.

Function: RecoveryRetryService.public RecoveryRetryService(OperationJournal journal, IFileSystem fileSystem, IClock clock, IRecycleBin? recycleBin = null, Func<bool>? allowPermanentDelete = null, FileActionService? fileActionGate = null)
Rationale: Null-checks journal, file system and clock; recycleBin, the permanent-delete setting reader and the INV-4 gate are optional and null means 'not allowed / no gate'; group Recycle paths guard a null bin before use. Tests: RecoveryRetryServiceTests, CompositionRootTests.

Function: RecoveryRetryService.public async Task<RecoveryRetryResult> RetryMoveOrCopyAsync(JournalEntry failed, bool confirmedFinishCancelled = false, CancellationToken ct = default)
Rationale: Takes the shared INV-4 gate before anything is read and returns the busy result (no journal, no mutation) if held; End() in finally only after a successful TryBegin; delegates to RetryCoreAsync. Tests: RecoveryRetryServiceTests, CaptureGroupActionServiceTests.

Function: RecoveryRetryService.private async Task<RecoveryRetryResult> RetryCoreAsync(JournalEntry failed, bool confirmedFinishCancelled, CancellationToken ct)
Rationale: CancelledByUser needs explicit confirmation; groups routed to RetryGroupAsync; single retry only for Move/Copy with a destination; source must exist with the exact journaled size and write time and the destination must not exist (IO-type errors become a failed result); prepared entry keeps Undo/Permanent via 'with'. The journal's destination is replayed without re-running ActionDestinationPolicy (W2-FA-08). Tests: RecoveryRetryServiceTests, RecoveryRetryCancelledTests.
Task.Run(() => ExecuteRetry(failed, prepared), ct): token only prevents starting; a started retry runs to completion and is journaled, so no half-state from cancellation.

Function: RecoveryRetryService.private async Task<RecoveryRetryResult> RetryGroupAsync(JournalEntry failed, CancellationToken ct)
Rationale: Checks: live id returns AlreadyHandled; RecoveryFileCheck must say CanRetry; pending members chosen per type; Recycle needs a bin and, for non-undo, the permanent-delete setting; each pending member re-verified against its fingerprint and destination absence; cumulative bin capacity re-checked. Defect (W2-FA-05): any verdict other than CanRetry (AlreadyDone, Lost, Conflict, DestinationChanged, Unknown) returns Tr.CoreRecoverySourceChanged ('source changed'), which is wrong text for e.g. an operation that already completed. Likely unreachable from the Recovery window (it offers retry only for CanRetry) except in races. Tests: RecoveryRetryGroupGapTests, RecoveryRecycleGroupTests.
Pending selector: Move/Copy members whose own verdict is CanRetry; Undo Recycle members whose source is Missing; Delete members that are NotRecycled; members already handled are left alone.

item => item.Member.Permanent used with FirstOrDefault: the first pending member that was journaled permanent is refused before any mutation unless the permanent-delete setting is on now. Test: RecoveryRecycleGroupTests.
item => item.Member projection feeding RecycleBinCapacity.FirstOverflow for the pending (not the whole) group, so a retry only needs room for what it will recycle. Test: RecoveryRecycleGroupTests.
Closure () => ExecuteGroupRetry(...) on the pool; token only gates start (and is checked between members inside).

Function: RecoveryRetryService.private RecoveryRetryResult ExecuteGroupRetry(JournalEntry failed, JournalEntry prepared, IReadOnlyList<RecoveryGroupMemberCheck> pending, CancellationToken ct)
Rationale: Transaction is retry-anchored (AppendIfUnchangedSince), live-id and Superseded handled; per member re-verifies fingerprints, destination absence and (Copy) uses CopyNewOrRemovePartial; ct checked between members; failure writes Failed with the same members (completed members then read as AlreadyDone). No rollback of already-retried members and no cleanup of a partial cross-volume Move destination (acceptable, Recovery shows it). The journal's destination/source paths are replayed without ActionDestinationPolicy or ValidateNoEscapeViaReparsePoint (W2-FA-08, not reproduced). Tests: RecoveryRetryGroupGapTests, RecoveryRecycleGroupTests, RecoveryRetryRaceTests.

Function: RecoveryRetryService.private void CopyNewOrRemovePartial(string source, string destination, long sourceSize)
Rationale: Create-new copy with a fresh proof; on a throw only a proven-created destination is removed and only while strictly shorter than the source, then the original exception is rethrown with throw; created==false raises destination-exists without touching the foreign file (R01 fixed by #290). Test: CopyForeignDestinationTests.
Returns the shared Superseded result (message CoreRecoveryAlreadyHandled, Entry null) so the caller drops its stale snapshot; no state touched.

Function: RecoveryRetryService.private RecoveryRetryResult ExecuteRetry(JournalEntry failed, JournalEntry prepared)
Rationale: Live check, retry-anchored Prepared, CreateDirectory of the destination folder, Copy through CopyNewOrRemovePartial plus VerifyDestination, Move plus VerifyMoved, Commit/Fail with Superseded handling; failures after MutationCompleted report the not-journaled message. Uses failed.Destination straight from the journal without re-running ActionDestinationPolicy/reparse checks (W2-FA-08, not reproduced). Tests: RecoveryRetryServiceTests, RecoveryRetryRaceTests, RecoveryRetryServiceMutationTests.

Function: RecycleBinCapacity.public static JournalGroupMember? FirstOverflow(IRecycleBin recycleBin, IEnumerable<JournalGroupMember> members)
Rationale: Groups non-permanent members by Path.GetPathRoot (OrdinalIgnoreCase, null root becomes empty string) and asks FitsInRecycleBin for the SUM of that volume's sizes using the first member's path; returns the first member of the first volume that does not fit; volumes mounted as folders share a root and are summed together (over-conservative refusal, never an unsafe accept). Test: RecycleBinCapacityGuardTests.
member => !member.Permanent: permanent members never use the bin, so they must not count against capacity.
member => Path.GetPathRoot(member.Source) ?? string.Empty groups by volume root; UNC roots (\\server\share) group per share.
member => member.Size summed as long; the sum of file sizes cannot overflow.

Function: UndoService.public UndoService( OperationJournal journal, IFileSystem fileSystem, IRecycleBin recycleBin, FileActionService? fileActionService = null, Func<string, string, Task>? moveOverride = null, IClock? clock = null)
Rationale: Null-checks journal/file system/bin; FileActionService is optional (shared INV-4 gate when supplied, own flag otherwise); clock defaults to SystemClock. Tests: UndoServiceTests.
Internal test seam returning the fingerprint dictionary count (asserts the map does not grow across register/undo cycles).
Exposes the mutable move stack; production code outside the class does not use it (grep: only tests), so there is no concurrent reader of a non-thread-safe Stack.
Returns the private UndoActionRecord boxed as object for the App's 'can undo' check; read-only reference.
Uses the shared FileActionService.IsBusy when present, otherwise its own volatile flag, so INV-4 covers undo and file actions together.
Delegates to FileActionService.TryBegin (single shared gate) or an Interlocked.CompareExchange on its private flag; atomic either way.
Releases the same gate that TryBegin took; callers call it only in finally after a successful TryBegin (verified in UndoMoveAsync, UndoLastAsync recycle branch and both group undos).

Ignores failed/rejected results; a Move registers the history entry, fingerprint (keyed by destination, case-insensitive) and last action; a Recycle registers a last action carrying PermanentlyDeleted; Copy registers nothing so an earlier undo stays available; unsynchronised state, but only the UI thread calls it after the action completes. Tests: UndoServiceTests.

Success needs journaled members; a FAILED Recycle group registers only completed members plus the Failed line so Ctrl+Z can restore what reached the bin; a failed Move or Copy registers nothing; Permanent is true only when every member was deleted permanently; falls back to members[0] when Entry is null. Tests: UndoServiceGroupTests.
member => member.Completed filter of a failed Recycle group's members, so a member still on disk is never offered for restore.
member => member.Member projection to the journaled identity (source, size, write time) that TryRestore matches against.
member => member.Permanent inside All(): the undo action is flagged permanent only when no member could be restored.

Gate first; pop; a missing destination is 'permanently broken' (dropped once), an existing source or any fingerprint mismatch (tolerant 2 s compare, journal fallback when absent) re-pushes the entry; the undo is journaled as a Move with Undo=true under a live marker, Failed on exception, Commit failure does not undo the move; fingerprint removed and last action cleared only when it is this Move. After a half-completed undo (move done, verify failed) the entry is pushed back and next time classed as broken, which is safe. Tests: UndoServiceTests, UndoServiceMutationGapTests.

x => x.Destination equals move.Destination (OrdinalIgnoreCase) over ReadCommittedMoves (which may include Undo=true lines whose Destination is an original source); only the fallback for callers that filled the public stack directly, not a normal path.

Task.Run(() => _fileSystem.Move(move.Destination, move.Source)): source absence was checked just before and Move does not overwrite, so a racing file at the source makes it throw and the entry is kept.

Dispatches on the last action: group Move/Recycle to their handlers, single Move to UndoMoveAsync (the history top is that Move by construction of Register/UndoMoveAsync), single Recycle: permanent gives a message and clears, busy gate, refuses when a file now exists at the original path, TryRestore with a tolerance for a restore that reports false although the identical file is back. The single Recycle restore is not journaled (group restore is). Tests: UndoServiceTests, UndoServiceGroupTests.
Task.Run(() => _recycleBin.TryRestore(path, size, lastWrite)): the slow bin enumeration is off the UI thread; exact identity match is the bin implementation's responsibility.

Function: UndoService.private async Task<UndoResult> UndoGroupMoveAsync(UndoActionRecord action, IReadOnlyList<JournalGroupMember> members)
Rationale: Builds undo members (destination-to-source), classifies each: both present throws, already back needs the moved file's fingerprint, otherwise the file at the old destination must match tolerantly; pending==0 resolves a partial undo or reports already handled; journals a group Undo Move Prepared under a marker, moves on the pool with per-member verification, commit, resolve partial, drop; failures remember restored members and keep the action for a Ctrl+Z retry. Tests: UndoServiceGroupTests, UndoServiceMutationGapTests.

member => new JournalGroupMember(member.Destination ?? throw IOException, member.Source, ...): a member without a Destination throws inside the try so the undo fails cleanly (CoreUndoSourceOrDestinationChanged) before any journaling; Permanent is intentionally not carried (irrelevant for Move).
member => member.Source for RestoredPaths when a retry finds everything already back (original paths for the catalog).

Pool lambda moving the pending members sequentially: CreateDirectory, move (override or file system), verify that the source is gone and the size matches, then record restored; restored/restoredByThisUndo are only mutated here and read after the await, so there is no concurrent access; cancellation not supported (no token).
member => member.Source for the success RestoredPaths (the original locations).

Function: UndoService.private void RememberPartialUndo(UndoActionRecord action, int restoredByThisUndo, JournalEntry? failedEntry)
Rationale: Stores the Failed lines of this action only when this undo restored something or an earlier partial for the SAME action reference exists, so an unrelated action's memory is not reused (ReferenceEquals); returns early otherwise.

Takes and clears the memory; only a partial for the same action closes its earlier Failed lines with Committed through AppendIfUnchangedSince (skipped if another writer touched the Id); all non-OOM exceptions swallowed because the undo itself is complete; returns true only when it resumed a partial. Tests: UndoServiceGroupTests.

Function: UndoService.private void SettleFailedDeleteLine(UndoActionRecord action, IReadOnlyCollection<string> restored)
Rationale: Best effort: replaces the Failed Delete line with a Failed line of the not-restored members or a Dismissed line, anchored on the latest line this action wrote; re-anchors only when the newer line is a Failed line over a subset of the original members; non-OOM exceptions swallowed. Tests: UndoServiceGroupTests, UndoServiceMutationGapTests.
Lambda over latestMembers.All(member => original.Any(...)): the outer predicate of the subset check that decides whether a newer Failed line is still 'ours'.
Inner predicate o => string.Equals(o.Source, member.Source, OrdinalIgnoreCase): case-insensitive path identity as everywhere else in this service.

Function: UndoService.private bool TrySettleFrom(UndoActionRecord action, JournalEntry anchor, IReadOnlyCollection<string> restored)
Rationale: Needs a members list; remaining = members not restored (case-insensitive); empty gives a Dismissed replacement, otherwise a Failed replacement with remaining[0] mirrored into the top-level fields; appended only while the anchor is still the latest (AppendIfUnchangedSince) and then becomes the new anchor.
member => !restored.Contains(member.Source, OrdinalIgnoreCase): selects members still on the Failed line.
ex is not OutOfMemoryException: deliberately swallows everything else (including cancellation) because settling is best effort and must never change the result of a finished undo.

Removes the fingerprints keyed by each member destination and clears the last action; group moves never populate the fingerprint map, so the removal is a harmless no-op that keeps symmetry; called only inside the gate by the undo that owns the action.

Function: UndoService.private async Task<UndoResult> UndoGroupRecycleAsync(UndoActionRecord action, IReadOnlyList<JournalGroupMember> members)
Rationale: Permanent action refused with a message; per member: permanent members are unrecoverable but do not block the rest, an existing file at the original path must be the recycled file itself (size and write time) else the undo stops; pending==0 resolves or reports already handled; journals a group Undo Recycle, restores each pending member through TryRestore with a FileExists post-check, settles the Failed Delete line, clears the action; failure keeps it and reports restored paths. pending>0 implies a non-permanent member, so undoMembers[0] exists. Tests: UndoServiceGroupTests.
member => !member.Permanent: the journaled undo covers only restorable members.
member => member with { }: shallow record copy so the journal entry does not alias the original manifest objects.
Pool lambda restoring each pending member: TryRestore must succeed and the file must exist afterwards, restored/restoredByThisUndo updated sequentially and read after the await.

Function: UndoService.private static string[] RestoredInOrder(IReadOnlyList<JournalGroupMember> members, IReadOnlyCollection<string> restored)
Rationale: Filters the manifest by the restored set (case-insensitive) so the returned order is the capture order, not the restore order.
member => restored.Contains(member.Source, OrdinalIgnoreCase): membership test for the ordered restored list.
member => member.Source projection of the restored members to paths.

Function: UndoService.private static string? UnrecoverableNote(IReadOnlyList<JournalGroupMember> members, IReadOnlyCollection<string> restored, List<JournalGroupMember> unrecoverable)
Rationale: Returns null unless at least one member could not be restored; the note counts restored versus total and lists unrecoverable file names (Path.GetFileName of journal paths, safe for any string).
member => Path.GetFileName(member.Source) for the unrecoverable names; GetFileName never throws on a non-null string.
